## UX review: skill pages a11y-audit, copy-tight, spec-writer Reviewed: The header and first section of three skill pages built from one template, given as code. Layout input: none. Main goal: install the skill shown on the page Steps to main goal: 1 (skill page: Copy install command) Findings: 2 (S1: 0, S2: 1, S3: 0, S4: 1) ### Findings 1. **Skill page template, header, on 3 pages: skills/a11y-audit.html, skills/copy-tight.html, skills/spec-writer.html** | S2 Major | R-ux-review-11 - Evidence: "Install" - User experiences: The user clicks Install in the header, expecting to install this skill, and lands on the collection page instead. - Recommendation: Make the one label "Install" name one action, so the header link no longer leads away from the skill the user is viewing. 2. **spec-writer page, Compare section, button** | S4 Note | R-ux-review-30 - Evidence: "

Compare

" - User experiences: The user sees a second primary install button under Compare and wonders which of the two to press. - Recommendation: Keep one primary action in the view and make the repeated install control secondary, or remove it. ### Not reviewed - Contrast, focus styles, spacing and type scales: a visual polish pass. - Semantics, ARIA and screen-reader output: an accessibility audit. - Wording of labels and messages: a copy edit. ### Open questions - Copy install command button (all pages): the input shows no visible confirmation after the click, and no script is given, so it is unknown whether "copied" is shown and what is copied. - Step after the copy (all pages): the input does not show where the user pastes the command or what they see afterwards. - Header "Install" target (all pages): the index page's install section is not given, so it is unknown whether it also installs this skill. - spec-writer page, two primary buttons: no layout is given, so it is unknown whether both appear in the same screen. - All targets and gaps (all pages): no sizes or gaps are given for the header links or buttons. - First screen and page length (all pages): no measurement sheet is given, so it is unknown who the first screen says the skill is for, or how tall each page is. ### Severity scale - S1 Blocker: the user cannot complete the main goal, or loses data or money. - S2 Major: the user completes the main goal only after a wrong action, an error or a second attempt. - S3 Minor: the user completes the main goal at the first attempt, but more slowly. - S4 Note: the result and the speed do not change; the place departs from the rule.
